oracle.method: enumeration of the structural noise cells with exact rational arithmetic
oracle.independence_basis: Enumerating the 4^4 (and 4^3) equally likely noise cells of each declared binary SCM, with exact rational arithmetic, evaluates the outcome equation under the assignment T = 1 on every cell, which gives the interventional law with no identification formula involved. The contingency tables are rebuilt from the same cells (each cell one observed row, counts divided by their gcd); the g-formula of each completion is applied to the table alone and must reproduce the structural truth (generating completion) or define the other completion's probability (the adjusted completion), and the per-atom lowest, highest and equal-weight mean over the two completions are derived from those. It imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated SCM, so a wrong coefficient in the fixture would be inherited.
asserted_outputs: class_point truth.y0 and truth.y1 (the interventional law under do(T=1))
class_disagree truth per-atom lower, upper and mean over the two completions
context_only_outputs: frequentist and bayesian estimator ids and tolerances
oracle.historical_exposure: The generator and its numbers were written during this review from the declared structural equations; the product's output was not consulted. Thresholds, tables and every value here are new.

reference_review.scope: Two binary structural models (a Markovian one with a root parent of the treatment, and a treatment-covariate pair whose edge a CPDAG leaves undirected): contingency tables, the interventional law, and the per-atom envelope over the two completions.

reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. Python standard library only, in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.
reference_review.limitations: Exact arithmetic on fixed tables; no sampling variability, no uncertainty or coverage claim. Graph classes, identification rules and estimator tolerances are context the generator cannot derive. The adjusted completion is derived from the observed law by its identification formula, not from a structural model that generated it. No calibration.
